text:
incident-bot: PAGING: streaming service p99 spike (eu-west-1) for /v1/streamed/generate — SLO breach detected. Alerts: p95 420ms (SLO 200ms), p99 1.8s (SLO 400ms). Auto-runbook triggered: `streaming-backpressure`.

alice_sre: seeing a big tail spike starting ~4210000000. dashboard shows concurrent connections up 2.8x and proxy write queue depth rising. customers reporting stalled streams. paging now.

bob_runtime: ACK. grabbing traces. initial hypothesis: slow consumers + proxy write buffer filling -> runtime backpressure cascade.

carol_prod: any impacted customers flagged? CS told a small payments customer saw stalled receipts. David, can you pull customer-facing notes?

david_support: confirmed two customers reported >30s stalls, one on EU prod. Not widespread but high severity for them. SEO-ticket created: INC-4210.

alice_sre: logs: 
```
proxy_write_queue=4820 avg_write_latency_ms=1200 socket_cwnd=64k kernel_qlen=4096
runtime_kv_cache_miss_rate=0.12 streaming_chunk_delay_ms_p50=120 p99=2400
```

alice_sre: tcp retransmits increasing on proxy -> looks like downstream slow readers (browser clients) causing socket backpressure.

eve_network: wire-level shows many connections in TCP_OFL (application paused) and some abrupt FINs. Could be a client-side issue; however proxy keepalive and chunk flush behavior might be exacerbating.

bob_runtime: pulling runtime traces: a subset of requests are sitting in the output queue waiting for flush; KV cache hit rate for these tails is low -> per-request latency amplifies. Also seeing contention on the write pump goroutine when queue depth > 2000.

bob_runtime: quick mitigation idea: enable conservative stream-shed policy on proxy to drop slowest connections and prioritize active ones, reduce proxy write buffer size to fail-fast, and route new requests to cold backfill pool.

carol_prod: product decision: prefer graceful degradation over dropping customers — try soft-throttle first then shed if necessary. Notify affected customers if we must drop.

alice_sre: mitigation step 1: enable `proxy.stream_shed=true` (soft) and `proxy.flush_interval_ms=50` (instead of 200). Applying now.

incident-bot: deploy started by alice_sre — rollout id: r-82134, target: eu-proxy-cluster-3. Rolling update in waves of 10%.

frank_oncall_next: I'm on standby for handoff, can take next shift in 30m.

bob_runtime: monitoring traces post-change. initial signal: write queue depth decreased from 4800 -> 900 in ~60s. p99 fell to ~900ms. Not at SLO yet but better.

alice_sre: applying mitigation step 2: enable routing override to dedicated warm pool (dedicated-eu-warm) for /v1/streamed/generate for customers with active sessions. This will split traffic: 30% -> dedicated pool.

incident-bot: routing change applied by alice_sre.

david_support: customer-facing note updated: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls in EU. Workaround: reconnecting usually resumes stream. We'll update once resolved." :thumbsup:

bob_runtime: still seeing some long tails. Running `strace` on the busiest proxy instance shows frequent `write()` returning EAGAIN and then repeated retries with small sleeps -> classic slow-reader problem.

eve_network: kernel parameters on proxy hosts: `net.ipv4.tcp_wmem` defaults look low for sustained bursts. Propose bumping send buffer on proxy nodes and enable `tcp_autotune_min` to higher lower bound.

alice_sre: I want to avoid kernel tune unless necessary. Try app-layer first. Next step: enable `keepalive_probe` more aggressively and reduce `proxy_write_retries` to fail faster so we can shed.

carol_prod: agree with app-layer first. Also need to prepare customer comms if we decide to hard-shed.

bob_runtime: small code change suggested: make the streaming write pump drop after N=3 EAGAINs instead of blocking for up to 1s. We can hot-toggle with feature flag `write_drop_threshold`.

alice_sre: enabling flag `write_drop_threshold=3` on proxy cluster. Deploying now (r-82135).

incident-bot: feature flag toggled by alice_sre.

bob_runtime: post-toggle we see p99 down to ~420ms, p95 ~180ms. SLOs close to recovery. Some clients saw an abrupt connection close — need to check logs for which user agents.

david_support: flagged customers that experienced abrupt closes to priority support. Adding mitigation script to help clients reconnect gracefully.

carol_prod: request to runtime: add metric `stream_drop_reason` with labels (eagain_retries, client_closed, proxy_drop) so we can quantify dropped connections for postmortem.

bob_runtime: will add counter and a small dashboard tile. ETA 2h. For now we have coarse logs.

eve_network: followup: still seeing occasional kernel queue bloat on node proxy-3b even after flag. Planning a rolling host reboot in 20m as last resort.

alice_sre: negative on reboots while traffic high. prefer draining conn + deploy replacement host. Starting drain of proxy-3b.

incident-bot: drain started on proxy-3b by alice_sre. new connections will avoid it.

frank_oncall_next: taking over primary oncall in 30m. Please leave a concise handoff note with what remains open.

alice_sre: Handoff note: issue: streaming p99 spike due to slow reader/backpressure. Actions taken: enabled stream_shed soft, decreased flush interval, routed 30% to dedicated warm pool, toggled write_drop_threshold=3, draining proxy-3b. Customer impact: two customers experienced stalls >30s; small number had abrupt reconnects after drop. Current state: p99 ~420ms, p95 ~180ms, system stable but watchlist for 2 hours. Next steps: add `stream_drop_reason` metric, investigate client UA patterns, consider kernel tuning if recurs.

carol_prod: I'll draft a customer update later tonight summarizing steps and expected follow-up.

david_support: I'll keep INC-4210 updated and coordinate customer callbacks.

bob_runtime: logging note: saved trace bundle to s3://redwood-incidents/4210000000/trace-bundle.tar.gz

incident-bot: INCIDENT: status=mitigated -> monitor. If p99 > 600ms again, auto-pager will escalate to oncall+runtime.

frank_oncall_next: ack. I'll monitor next 2 hours, will take full oncall at 4210001800. Leaving a reminder to follow up on metric addition and postmortem.

alice_sre: thanks team. quick retrospective: look for correlated client library versions and proxy instances; add regression test to simulate many slow readers and verify stream-shed behavior.

incident-bot: thread closed for now. Please re-open if regressions observed.
